chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Bakr ibn Salih, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Abdullah ibn Ja'far ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Whoever clothes one of the poor Muslims with a garment to cover his nakedness, or assists him with something from what sustains his livelihood, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will assign to him seven thousand angels from among the angels who seek forgiveness for every sin he has committed, until the Trumpet is blown.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for clothing a poor Muslim according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to emphasize the immense spiritual merit of clothing a poor Muslim, linking material generosity directly to divine intercession. The specific reward of seven thousand angels seeking forgiveness for every sin committed until the Trumpet is blown underscores the permanence of this reward in Shia eschatology, extending beyond the grave until the final resurrection.
